studies.Reference: Adipose tissue omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acid content and breast cancer in the EURAMIC study. European Community Multicenter Study on Antioxidants, Myocardial Infarction, and Breast Cancer.
studies.Authors: Simonsen N, van't Veer P, Strain JJ, Martin-Moreno JM, Huttunen JK, Navajas JF, Martin BC, Thamm M, Kardinaal AF, Kok FJ, Kohlmeier L
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: The fatty acid content of adipose tissue in postmenopausal breast cancer cases and controls from five European countries.

extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: In Malaga, Spain, the odds ratio for the highest tertile relative to the lowest reached 0.32 (95% confidence interval 0.13-0.82).
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: The ratio of long-chain omega-3 fatty acids to total omega-6 fat showed an inverse association with breast cancer in four of five centers.
extraction_supporting_text.p_value: A downward trend bordering on statistical significance (p for trend = 0.055).
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: Breast cancer incidence in postmenopausal women.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Fatty acid content of adipose tissue, specifically omega-6 polyunsaturates.

studies.Reference: Total Dietary Fats, Fatty Acids, and Omega-3/Omega-6 Ratio as Risk Factors of Breast Cancer in the Polish Population - a Case-Control Study.
studies.comparison_type: Low omega-3/omega-6 ratio (<0.2) vs. higher ratio
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Detailed dietary intake information was assessed using a validated Food Frequency Questionnaire.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: A total of 201 consecutive, newly diagnosed, polish female cancer patients ... and 201 one-to-one age-matched controls were enrolled.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Low (<0.2) omega-3/ omega-6 ratio ... were associated with increased risk of breast cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: Breast cancer is the most common type of cancer among women

studies.Reference: Polyunsaturated fatty acid interactions and breast cancer incidence: a population-based case-control study on Long Island, New York.
studies.Authors: Khankari NK, Bradshaw PT, Steck SE, He K, Olshan AF, Shen J, Ahn J, Chen Y, Ahsan H, Terry MB, Teitelbaum SL, Neugut AI, Santella RM, Gammon MD
studies.comparison_type: low ω-3/high ω-6 vs high ω-3/low ω-6

extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Breast cancer risk reduction may be possible for U.S. women with dietary consumption of higher ω-3, which has anti-inflammatory properties, in concert with lower ω-6, which induces inflammation.

studies.Reference: ω-3 and ω-6 Polyunsaturated fatty acid intakes and the risk of breast cancer in Mexican women: impact of obesity status.
studies.Authors: Chajès V, Torres-Mejía G, Biessy C, Ortega-Olvera C, Angeles-Llerenas A, Ferrari P, Lazcano-Ponce E, Romieu I
studies.Journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Women provided information on health and diet by in-person interview.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: A population-based case-control study was conducted in Mexico, including 1,000 incident breast cancer cases and 1,074 controls.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: An increased risk of breast cancer was associated with increasing ω-6 PUFA intake in premenopausal women [OR = 1.92, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.13-3.26; P = 0.04].
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: An increased risk of breast cancer was associated with increasing ω-6 PUFA intake in premenopausal women.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: We evaluated the association between ω-3 and ω-6 PUFA intake and breast cancer risk.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: ω-6 PUFA intake was assessed through dietary information provided by in-person interview.

headline.funnel_interpretation: The significant funnel plot asymmetry (egger's p=0.0430) indicates substantial publication bias in this meta-analysis on omega-6 fatty acids and breast cancer. This specific pattern suggests that smaller studies with smaller or null effects may be underrepresented, compromising the reliability of the pooled estimate and potentially leading to an overestimation of the true association.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 4 studies yielded an overall effect size of 1.61 (95% CI: 1.17–2.2), suggesting that omega-6 fatty acids is associated with a higher risk of breast cancer. However, this association should be interpreted with caution, as there was substantial between-study heterogeneity (I² = 50.19%), reflecting considerable variability across studies.
